title: How does adolescent neurodevelopment impact substance use? The substance use neuroplasticity and peer (SNAP) model: A novel neurodevelopmental model of adolescent substance use
title_zh: 青春期神经发育如何影响物质使用？物质使用神经可塑性与同伴（SNAP）模型：青春期物质使用的新型神经发育模型
abstract: Substance use among adolescents age 13-18 remains a significant societal concern, yet contemporary neuroscience models of addiction have been grounded in the chronic, cyclic stage model developed for adult presentations of substance use disorder (SUD). Relative to adults, adolescents exhibit distinct patterns of substance use, and many structural and functional findings garnered from studies of addiction in the adult brain have not been reliably observed or replicated in adolescent samples. Thus, contemporary models of adult addiction do not readily translate to adolescents, resulting in downstream developmental incongruities in how substance use is conceptualized, measured, and treated in this age group. Here, we present a review of the current state of human and preclinical models of neurobiological risk factors and mechanisms specific to substance use in adolescents. Grounded in this literature, we present the Substance use Neuroplasticity And Peer (SNAP) model, a novel neurodevelopmental model of adolescent substance use that captures the differentiated nature of substance use initiation and escalation in this high-need, yet undertreated population.
abstract_zh: 13-18 岁青少年中的物质使用仍是重大的社会关注点，但当代神经科学的成瘾模型主要基于针对成人物质使用障碍（SUD）的慢性、循环阶段模型。与成人相比，青少年表现出不同的物质使用模式，且许多来自成人成瘾研究的结构和功能发现未能在青少年样本中可靠观察或复制。因此，成人成瘾的现代理论难以直接迁移到青少年，导致在该年龄组如何概念化、测量和治疗物质使用时出现发展不匹配。本文综述了针对青少年物质使用的神经生物学风险因素和机制的当前人类与前临床模型。基于此文献，我们提出了物质使用神经可塑性与同伴（SNAP）模型，这是一种新颖的青春期神经发育模型，捕捉了这一高需求但治疗不足人群中物质使用启动和升级的差异化特征。
